subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella stay open until both the guarded retention cleanup and warning/context guardrail slices are resolved, or should maintainers split the remaining guardrails into narrower canonical issues now?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but warning thresholds, context-pressure warnings, and base-session cleanup semantics are compatibility-sensitive product choices rather than one safe automatic repair.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Settle
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers choose the retention PR path and the advisory policy, then split only leftovers after those decisions.

options.title: Split Remaining Guardrails
options.body: Create or confirm separate canonical issues for context-threshold warnings, high-frequency warnings, and sessions cleanup, then let each PR close only its own slice.

options.title: Narrow To Retention Only
options.body: Treat the warning threshold as not planned or separately sponsored, and keep only the source-reproducible retention cleanup work active.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Until Slices Settle
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while maintainers choose the retention PR path and the advisory policy, then split only leftovers after those decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the cron/session lifecycle boundary introduced and maintained around the reaper path.
